note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/sign-in.reason: cinatra#2754 (PR #2895 carries this record; the ruling on the issue names the mechanism): the single-use island-grant ledger gains ONE module, and it sits on the shared store surface, so it is reachable from every locked route that mounts the store: +1 on all five routes, including /sign-in (the auth surface reads the same store). src/lib/lifecycle/review-island-grant-store.ts — the hash-keyed grant ledger whose atomic spend semantics are unit-assertable against a ledger stand-in without loading the server-only store graph; inlining it into the store was rejected because the spend-once property must be testable in isolation and the file-size ratchet holds the store's ceiling flat. Measured with the pinned extension tree.

/api/mcp.reason: cinatra#2882 (PR #2884 carries this record; the reason names the issue): the async notification seam's query runner, src/lib/postgres-async.ts, is ONE new module on the graph of every locked route that reaches the notifications host: +1 on these four routes, /sign-in unchanged. It is reached from src/lib/notifications-host.ts — the SINGLE production registrant of the notifications host adapters, and already on all four graphs at the base — through a literal `await import("@/lib/postgres-async")`. Neither documented narrowing applies: there is no barrel to swap for a concrete module (this IS the concrete module), and the import cannot be made unreachable from these routes, because the module holding it is the adapter registrant these routes already load. The round's OTHER +1 was narrowed away rather than absorbed: the seam's own packages/notifications/src/service-async.ts was folded into packages/notifications/src/service.ts — which it already imported, and which these routes already load — taking this raise from +2 to +1. The remaining module is not foldable the same way. Its only already-counted candidate host is @/lib/db/pooled, a 194-line lazy-pool factory shared by ~two dozen stores, and postgres-async.ts is a 330-line query runner with its own env-read ceiling, int32 clamp, and transaction/rollback semantics — the deliberate sibling of @/lib/postgres-sync, kept separate from the pool it borrows.

/chat.reason: An EXPIRED schedule proposal must stay VISIBLE with an Adjust that re-proposes, instead of resolving to the undrawn state reserved for a reader who may not see the subject. Drawing a reading that did not exist before costs this route FOUR modules, and these are the four, enumerated by name because the count and the list have to agree: (1) packages/chat/src/renderable-views/trigger-schedule-proposal-expired.tsx, the expired reading's own component; and the three the Adjust edge pulls in behind it, (2) packages/agents/src/trigger-schedule-proposal-actions.ts, the server-action module the press handler reaches, (3) packages/agents/src/trigger-schedule-proposal-service.ts and (4) packages/agents/src/trigger-schedule-proposal-store.ts, which that action module imports in turn. Exactly three for the action edge because this route already carries the session graph the action sits on, and the action is reached through a DYNAMIC import inside the press handler so the confirm and propose half stays off the initial graph. The kind's view-schema leaf, packages/agent-ui-protocol/src/renderable-views/trigger-schedule-proposal-view.ts, costs this route NOTHING and is deliberately not in the list: it was already reachable from /chat before this change, and after rebasing onto S9c's resolve envelope (PR #2795) the shell no longer imports it at RUNTIME at all — the envelope is parsed once at the protocol's own seam and the shell reads an already-typed body, so its only remaining protocol import is type-only and erased. An earlier revision of this record named that leaf as one of the four, which made the count and the enumeration disagree by one; the enumeration above is measured as the reachable-module set difference between this head and origin/main, with the companion extension tree cloned pinned on BOTH sides (1795 -> 1799), and it is exactly these four and nothing else. The 1795 base is PR #2884's ceiling, whose own absorb record this one supersedes on the same route. No other locked route moves. The alternatives were rejected: a dedicated API route for one button widens the surface more than the modules it would save; folding Adjust into an actions module already on this graph would undo the split that keeps the confirm transaction and the install outbox off the five locked MCP route graphs; and leaving the card undrawn is the defect itself. The reading is drawn once, in the shell every declared host already renders, so it costs no new host mount.
